---
title: "ssoossh ssh proxycommand"
description: "Ensure a valid certificate, then hand the connection to a relay command such as nc."
---

<!-- Generated by genclidocs from the cobra command tree in client/cmd. Do not edit. -->

For use as ssh_config's ProxyCommand. Ensures a valid certificate is in your ssh-agent, then hands the connection to the relay command that follows it. Write the relay command exactly as you would without ssoossh:

    Before: ProxyCommand /usr/bin/nc -X connect -x 192.0.2.0:8080 %h %p
    After:  ProxyCommand ssoossh ssh proxycommand /usr/bin/nc -X connect -x 192.0.2.0:8080 %h %p

Everything from the relay command on is passed to it unparsed, so put ssoossh flags such as --server, --config or -v before it.

Requires an ssh-agent: ssh reads key files once, at startup, so a certificate written to disk afterwards would never be used. Without an agent, use the Match exec recipe from `ssoossh ssh config`.

## Synopsis

```
ssoossh ssh proxycommand <command> [args...]
```

## Global options

Inherited from [`ssoossh`](/ssoossh/reference/cli/ssoossh/) and its parents.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-c`, `--config` | string |  | path to an extra config file, merged after the standard locations |
| `--server` | string |  | server address, e.g. https://ssh.example.com; https is assumed when no scheme is given |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | count | `0` | trace what the command is doing, to stderr; repeat for more (-v steps, -vv requests and files, -vvv bodies) |
